packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-16 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. The only text seen beyond the images is a modern pencil shelfmark on the leaf itself ("Stams, StA, Frg. 108?c" or similar, top right of face 1), which names the holding but not the work.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of face 1)
- Small irregular strip of parchment, roughly 13 cm wide x 5-6 cm high against the scale; torn on all sides, with a large bite out of the lower edge in the middle.
- Orientation: text upright as photographed.
- Ten or so lines of a small Gothic textualis/cursiva-influenced book hand in brown ink, one column visible (left margin edge appears at left on some lines; no second column seen). Line ends at right appear cut by the tear, so line length is unknown.
- Red ink: a red paragraph mark / red-touched capital mid-line around line 6 (near "...Alb..."), red stroke near line 2 ("&" area?), red at the bottom right ("Ub..."?). Some initials appear touched in red. No running title visible; top margin has the pencil shelfmark only.
- No interlinear or marginal glosses visible at overview scale.
- Content guess (tentative, from overview only): continuous prose with astronomical-looking vocabulary (planet-, signis?), but this is unconfirmed until the tiles are read.

FACE 1, LEFT TILE: image-002.jpg (native resolution; left c. 60% of the strip)
Observed: 8 text lines; the left edge of the writing block is visible on lines 2-5 (lines 1, 6-8 begin in the tear). Line 4 opens with a capital D touched in red; line 3 ends at the tile edge with a red-touched letter; line 5 has a red mark/initial (red "¶"-like stroke or red capital) at the right edge of the tile, joined to "Al..." (continues into image-003). Lines 7-8 are cut by the bite in the lower edge; line 8 is the last line on this part of the fragment.
Hand: small Gothic book hand with cursive features (long s and f descend below the line; 2-shaped r; "&"-like "et"; "9" for con-; "q3"/"aq3" for -que; z-like terminal sign that may be -m or -et).
Line numbers counted from the top of image-002.

002-01  [tear]i manentium(?) se[.]aute(?) et ortu(?)e(?) suste[ tile edge
         (first word: "imanētiu(m)" with a bar; could be "-manentium" or "-manencium"; "se" then 1-2 lost letters then "aute"/"ante"; "ortie"/"ortue" uncertain)
002-02  m(at)'ia (= materia?) et sum[.]is(?) 3 celeste(?) soli(?) velo[ tile edge
         ("celeste" could be "celestis"/"celestre"; the "3"-shaped sign after "sum.." is clear but its value uncertain; "velo" possibly beginning "velocit-")
002-03  sustatas(?) tēm(?) machinaz(?) Quia m(u)ndi [red-touched initial, perhaps O/C] [tile edge
         ("sustatas" could be an abbreviation of "substantias"; second word has a bar, "tantum"/"totum"? ; "machina(m)" with z-like final; "Quia" has a capital Q)
002-04  Dudum (red-touched D) i[.] munita(?)/mutac(?) tāt(?) celi q(uam)(?) terre [.]u[ tile edge
         (second word reads letter by letter "iȝ munca" / "ii munc a"; I cannot settle it; "q" with a bar over it before "terre")
002-05  seo(?) o ta(?) mot(us)(?) Dulassaq3(?) media(?) [red ¶ / red initial] Al[ tile edge
         ("Dulass..aq3": letters D-u-l-a-long s-long s-a-q-3, perhaps a -que word; uncertain)
002-06  [tear]nci(?) quidem(?) planete motu [abbr. mark] suu(?) q(ue)(?)[ tile edge
         ("quidez" = quidem; "planete" clear; "motu" clear)
002-07  [tear]9tra (= contra) ſ(e)p(ar)aiu(?) ulterior(?)/ultima(m)(?) [tear
         (second word: double long s / ff with a bar through the ascenders, then "aiu"; third word "ulti..z")
002-08  [tear]l̄ motus plan[ tear
         ("plan" then torn; "planet-" likely from context but not visible)

FACE 1, RIGHT TILE: image-003.jpg (native resolution; right c. 60% of the strip; overlaps image-002 by roughly the "suste-/velo-/mundi/terre/media" zone)
Observed: modern pencil shelfmark in top margin "Stams, StA, Frg. 108n" (letter after 108 read as n; could be another letter). Writing reaches to near the torn right edge; on lines 1-6 the line ends look like true line ends close to a right margin (text stops before the parchment edge), so this may be the right edge of the column. The fragment extends lower here than on the left: 11 lines in total, the last two very damaged. Red: a red stroke through a capital in line 1 ("[H?]ic"), red-touched U/V in line 3 ("Unde") and red-touched A in "Athanasius", large red capital/paragraph sign before "Al..." in line 5, red-touched N? in line 7 and P in line 7, red-touched V/U in line 10 ("Uale..."), red trace at the bottom edge.
Line numbers counted from the top of image-003 text (line 1 = the line with "sustentan..."; it is the same physical line as 002-01).

003-01  [overlap with 002-01: ...ortue(?)] sustentantur(?) [red-touched capital]ic (= Hic?) firmam(en)ti
         ("sustentan" then 2-3 letters, "-tur"/"-ter" uncertain; "firmamēti" with bar clear)
003-02  [overlap: ...soli(?) velo-] velo. with superscript "te"/"ce" (velo(citate)?) Quod(?) tm̄ (tamen?/tantum?) anulus(?)/aurolis(?) statu(?)/spacio(?)
         (the two words after "Quod" are uncertain: first "tm̄"/"tn̄"; second "auroly"/"amoly"; last "ſtaſu"/"ſpaſu")
003-03  [overlap: ...m(u)ndi] [red-touched U/O]nde (= Unde) [red-touched A]thanasi9 (= Athanasius) in sermone
         (clear; "in sermone" ends the line at the margin)
003-04  [overlap: ...q(uam)] terre [.]uisset(?)/nusset(?) mach(i)na si no(n) sustētaſ[ (sustentasset? / sustentaret?)
         ("machina" written "macha" with bar; "si nō" clear)
003-05  [overlap: ...media(?)] [large red initial/¶]Alkabici9 (= Alkabicius?) in ysagoica (= ysagogica?) planetas(?)
         (initial red letter looks like a red "q"/¶ shape with A; "Allkabiciq" letter by letter; "plan̄tas"/"planetis" uncertain at the end)
003-06  [overlap: ...motu ¯suu(?)] q(ue)(?)/q(uam) sunt(?)/suu faciunt v(ir)tu(te)(?)/vni9(?) firmam(en)ta(?)
         ("fiunt"/"faciunt": reads "facīūt"; the word before "firmama" with bar reads "vno"/"v'zo" with superscript: uncertain)
003-07  [tear] [red-touched N?]am(?) ut refert [red-touched P]h(?)[.]m(?)/Ptho(?) ...[
         ("ut refert" clear; the word after it begins with a red-touched P and has a bar; I cannot expand it)
003-08  [tear] toti(?) vniuersu(m)/vniuerso se in[.][
         ("totū"/"toti" then "vniusū" with bar = universum?; "se" clear; then "in" + lost)
003-09  [tear] et ho(m)i(nu)m(?) desideri[um?][
         ("hoīu" with marks = hominum?; "desideri" + lost)
003-10  [tear, faint letters with superscript: "...rna"/"...ma"] [red-touched V]ale(?)/Uale[
003-11  [tear] [.]o x̄p̄i (= Christi?) p̄s/p̄f [red trace][tear
         (very damaged; only "xpi" with bar fairly sure)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-004, overview of face 2)
- Same strip, other face (the bite in the lower edge is now right of centre, i.e. mirrored, consistent with the reverse). Pencil shelfmark top right "Stams, StA, Frg. 108v" (?).
- About 10-11 lines of the same hand in one visible column; left edge of writing visible on most lines; right side torn.
- Red: several red paragraph marks / red-touched capitals mid-line (line 1 "In...", line 2 right "¶ Si/Sil", line 4 "Ba/Ro", line 6 "Consistio..."?), more frequent than on face 1, suggesting short sections or quotations introduced by rubricated capitals.
- No running title, glosses or marginalia seen at this scale.

FACE 2, LEFT TILE: image-005.jpg (native resolution; left c. 60% of face 2)
Observed: 11 lines (counting a last line of 1-2 letter fragments with red at the bottom edge). Left edge of the writing block visible on lines 1-6; lines 7-11 begin close to the torn edge. Red-touched capitals: "In" (line 1), "Mulier" (line 3), "Constantinus" (line 6), "Hic"/"Eic"(?) (line 7); red traces at the lower-left edge on lines 10-11. Mid-line punctus with a raised point used before red capitals (line 3 "...· Mulier", line 6 "...· Bened-"). A wide blank top margin above line 1 (no running title).
Line numbers counted from the top of image-005.

005-01  anshelm(us)(?) 9(?) in sermone [red-touched I]n auct(?)is(?)/auct(ori)t(ate)(?) s[ tile edge
         (first word letter by letter "anſhelu" with a mark, then a small 9/q-like sign; "insermoe" = in sermone with bar)
005-02  dum(?)/dinis(?) cont(ra)(?) demonez (= demones/demonem) · omnez (= omnes/omnem) ei9 (= eius) i(n) n[ tile edge
         (first word "dmns"/"dums"; "cont'" with a hook)
005-03  bona(?)/baret(?) deser(i)t(?) i(n)terim(?)/intrum(?) · [red-touched M]ulier debili[s?][ tile edge
         ("Mulier" clear with red stroke; "debili" clear)
005-04  c(on)spicit(?) / ospiciat(?) insil[.]brium(?)/infirmitatem(?) suis(?) ipsius(?) frangit(?)/fragit [ tile edge
         (the second word is a run of minims and long s/l/b I cannot settle; "frāgit" with bar likely = frangit)
005-05  oc(u)la(?) with superscript "e"(?) nisi(?) with superscript [.] femine(?) comestum(?)/comestiui(?) puero(rum)(?)/pueros(?)[ tile edge
         ("femine" begins with tall f; "puer..." clear start)
005-06  q(ue)admodum (written "qadmodu" with marks) refert [red-touched C]onstantinus (Constatin9 with bar) · Bened[ tile edge
         (the citation formula "quemadmodum refert Constantinus" is clear)
005-07  [.]e(?) expallescat (= expallescat/expallescit) [red-touched H?/C?/E]ic(?) n(ost)r(?)/uir(?)[ tear
005-08  [.]mnaz/nnaz (= -mam?) feliciss(im)e (feliciſſīe with bar) de[i?]/deo(?)[ tear
005-09  [.]ias(?) : te ad apic[em](?) / ad apis(?) [.] [ tear
005-10  [red trace] [.]iq(ue)(?) m(en)te(?)/m(at)re(?) m[ tear
005-11  [red traces] h[.]c(?) [tear; only fragments of 2-3 letters]

FACE 2, RIGHT TILE: image-006.jpg (native resolution; right c. 60% of face 2; overlaps image-005 in the "auct-/eius/debilis/frangit/puer-/Bened-" zone)
Observed: pencil shelfmark in top margin "Stams, STA, Frg. 108v". 8 lines on this tile; the right edge is torn and line ends are lost on most lines (unlike face 1, I see no clear right margin here; lines 1-2 reach the tear). A large red paragraph-mark / red initial stroke at the right end of line 2 before "[.]hil/Sil"; red-touched R(?) and a separate red stroke before "Nam" in line 4; red-touched T(?) in line 8. Lines 7-8 survive only right of the lower bite.
Line numbers counted from the top of image-006 text (line 1 = same physical line as 005-01).

006-01  [overlap: In] auct(or)e (auct'o with superscript) salutis mee 7 (= et) turris fortitu[ tear
         (clear except the abbreviation of the first word)
006-02  [overlap: ...omnez] ei9 i(n) nobis ta(?)/tm̄(?) primus(?) diuinitate(?) [large red ¶/initial] [.]hil(?)/Sil(?)[ tear
         ("i nob" with bar = in nobis; "primus" reads "p'mus"; "Diuinitate" with capital-like D; last word begins with a letter partly painted over in red)
006-03  [overlap: Mu]lier debilis et infirma sep̄(?)/sexu(?) · sp(eci)al(ite)r(?) q(uo)d
         ("infirma" written "infra/infma" with long s; "Spe'alr" with a mark; "qd" with bar)
006-04  [overlap: ...ipsius] frangit [red-touched R]o(?) c(?) [red stroke][N]am quedam(?)/quidem(?) [.]factura(?)/ifectiua(?)[ tear
         ("Ro c" may be a reference abbreviation; "Naz" = Nam clear; the last word letter by letter "ifectua" with long s/f uncertain)
006-05  [overlap: ...comestiu]m puer(?)orum(?)/pueris(?) c(or)p(or)is frigiss(im)e(?)/frigidissime(?) i(n) media q[ tear
         ("corpis" with p-stroke = corporis; "ſrigiſſ" + z-like sign; "i media" + q)
006-06  [overlap: Constatin]9 · Benedicta(?)/Benedictus(?) cui9 (= cuius) multo(?) infirmorum(?)/infirmazo(?) [.][ tear
006-07  [tear] [.]u(?) sibi frangit et a[ tear
006-08  [tear] [.]ne aie (= anime) [red-touched T?/I?]ria(?)/Iua(?) a[.][ tear

SELECTED / UNREAD AREAS AND LIMITATIONS
- Read: every line visible on both faces, at least letter by letter. Firmer spans: face 1 lines 3-5 right half ("Unde Athanasius in sermone", "machina si non sustent-", "Alkabicius(?) in ysagoica planet-"), face 1 lines 6-9 right half ("faciunt ... firmament-", "ut refert", "universum se in-", "et hominum desideri-"); face 2 lines 1-6 ("in sermone In auctore salutis mee et turris fortitu-", "Mulier debilis et infirma ... specialiter quod", "quemadmodum refert Constantinus · Bened-", "corporis ... in media").
- Weak or unresolved: face 1 lines 1-2 left half (first words, the "3"-sign), face 1 line 4 second word, face 1 line 5 "Dulass..aq3", face 1 lines 10-11; face 2 line 2 first word, line 4 second word, line 5 "comestum/commestiui", lines 7-11 left half.
- Tiles overlap by roughly the middle third of each face; I matched lines across the overlap by the shared words noted in brackets and did not count repeated words twice.
- The fragment is a strip torn on all sides; only one column is visible on each face and its full width and line length are unknown. Face 1 may show the right margin (lines 1-6 end short of the tear); face 2 shows the left margin. Which face is recto is not established by the images.
- Structural observation: both faces carry rubricated capitals introducing short units, several of them names followed by "in sermone" / "refert" (Athanasius, Alkabicius(?), Anselmus(?), Constantinus, "Ro c"?), i.e. a text built from cited authorities. This is an interpretation of the layout, not an identification.
- A wider or raking-light view of face 1 lines 1-2 and face 2 lines 9-11 might help with the faint letters.
- Beyond the rules: I made enlarged crops (PIL) of each tile in the session scratchpad (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aaymeloglu--claude-assistant/e815e015-b31e-41c2-a426-393753ef7331/scratchpad/p16_*.png) and viewed them; nothing else was opened. I did not hit the image limit.
